artworks.title: Bacchus
artworks.description: An oil painting of the youthful wine god reclining with a shallow glass of wine, crowned with vine leaves and offering the cup to the viewer. Caravaggio paints Bacchus as a fleshy, faintly drowsy adolescent beside a basket of overripe fruit, mingling sensuality with hints of decay. The work hangs in the Uffizi Gallery in Florence.

artworks.title: Bacchus and Ariadne
artworks.description: A masterpiece of Venetian Renaissance painting in which Bacchus leaps from his cheetah-drawn chariot toward Ariadne, abandoned by Theseus on the shore of Naxos. The circle of stars above her alludes to her crown, set among the constellations. Painted for Alfonso d'Este's camerino in Ferrara, it now hangs in the National Gallery, London.

artworks.title: Bacchus
artworks.description: A marble statue carved by the young Michelangelo, showing a swaying, drunken Bacchus raising his cup while a small satyr nibbles at the grapes behind him. The deliberately unsteady pose captures intoxication in stone, a daring conceit for its time. The sculpture is in the Museo Nazionale del Bargello in Florence.

artworks.title: The Dionysus Cup
artworks.description: An Attic black-figure drinking cup (kylix) by the painter Exekias, showing Dionysus reclining in a ship whose mast sprouts grapevines, surrounded by dolphins. The scene evokes the Homeric Hymn in which the god, captured by Tyrrhenian pirates, transforms his captors into dolphins. The cup is held by the Staatliche Antikensammlungen in Munich.

music.title: L'Arianna
music.description: Monteverdi's lost opera for the Gonzaga court survives chiefly in Ariadne's lament — the cry of the woman Bacchus will claim on Naxos, the wine god arriving as consolation after Theseus' sail.

music.title: Bacchus and Ariadne
music.description: Roussel's ballet for the Paris Opéra retells the Naxos rescue in bright, neo-classical colour — Dionysus' arrival as choreography rather than tragedy.

popCulture.title: Hades
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: Dionysus' boons are hangover and festive fog — the wine god as a party build, cheering Zagreus on from Olympus between cups.

popCulture.title: Hades II
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: He returns among the Olympian boon-givers in the sequel, still the god of revels in a war that has little time for revels.
